## Comment System Architecture Summary

### 1. Backend Comment Routes and Handlers

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/routes/comment.routes.ts`**

The comment API provides these endpoints:

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/comments` | POST | Create a new comment on a text range |
| `/api/comments/:commentId/replies` | POST | Add a reply to an existing comment |
| `/api/comments/:commentId` | PATCH | Update comment (resolve/unresolve) |
| `/api/comments/:commentId` | DELETE | Delete a comment (author only) |

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/routes/repository.routes.ts`** (lines 378-453)

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/repositories/:owner/:repo/comments` | GET | Fetch all comments for a document |

### 2. Comment Data Models/Types

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/services/comment-file.service.ts`**

```typescript
// Author information
interface CommentAuthor {
  username: string;
  avatarUrl: string | null;
}

// Reply to a comment (flat structure - no nested replies)
interface CommentReply {
  id: string;           // Generated with nanoid: "r-{id}"
  author: CommentAuthor;
  text: string;
  createdAt: string;
}

// Main comment entity
interface DocumentComment {
  id: string;           // Generated with nanoid: "c-{id}"
  charStart: number;    // Start character position in document
  charEnd: number;      // End character position in document
  author: CommentAuthor;
  text: string;
  resolved: boolean;
  createdAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
  replies: CommentReply[];  // Flat array of replies (NO parent_id)
}

// Comment file structure
interface CommentFileData {
  version: number;
  documentPath: string;
  comments: DocumentComment[];
}
```

**Key observation: There is NO `parent_id` or nested reply structure.** Replies are stored as a flat array within each comment. This is a single-level threading model (comments have replies, but replies cannot have sub-replies).

### 3. Frontend Comment Components

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/CommentSidebar.tsx`**
- Main sidebar panel showing all comments for a document
- Displays comment threads with author, timestamp, text
- Shows replies nested under each comment
- Provides Reply, Resolve/Unresolve, Delete actions
- Polls for updates every 10 seconds
- Filters by resolved/unresolved status

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/AddCommentModal.tsx`**
- Modal for creating new comments
- Shows selected text preview with character range
- Submits to `/api/comments` endpoint

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/CommentHighlights.tsx`**
- Renders visual highlights in the editor for commented text ranges
- Uses mirror-div technique for accurate positioning
- Supports active/resolved state styling
- Clickable to navigate to comment in sidebar

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/EditorLayout.tsx`** (integration)
- Coordinates comment components
- Manages comment state and sidebar visibility
- Handles bi-directional navigation (sidebar <-> editor highlights)

### 4. Comment Storage

**Storage Location:** GitHub repository in `.mume/` folder

Comments are stored as **YAML frontmatter files** directly in the GitHub repository:
- Storage path: `.mume/{documentPath}` (e.g., `.mume/README.md`, `.mume/docs/guide.md`)
- File format: YAML frontmatter + Markdown body

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/services/github.service.ts`** (lines 757-833)

Key methods:
- `getCommentFile()` - Fetches comment file from GitHub (returns null if not exists)
- `saveCommentFile()` - Creates or updates comment file in GitHub

**Example comment file structure:**
```yaml
---
version: 1
documentPath: README.md
comments:
  - id: c-abc123
    charStart: 0
    charEnd: 50
    author:
      username: johndoe
      avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/123
    text: This introduction could be clearer
    resolved: false
    createdAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    updatedAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    replies:
      - id: r-xyz789
        author:
          username: janedoe
          avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/456
        text: I agree, let me revise it
        createdAt: 2024-01-01T01:00:00.000Z
---

# Comments for README.md

This file contains review comments for the associated document.
Do not edit manually - managed by the collaborative editor.
```

**Note:** The archived SQL migrations (`003_create_comments_table.sql`, `004_create_comment_replies_table.sql`) indicate there was once a PostgreSQL-based approach, but the current implementation uses GitHub as the source of truth.

### 5. Real-Time Sync Mechanism

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/server.ts`**

The real-time sync uses **Yjs with WebSocket (y-websocket)**:
- WebSocket server runs on the same port as the HTTP server (default: 3000)
- Uses `y-websocket/bin/utils` for connection handling
- Document name is extracted from the WebSocket URL path

**Frontend hook: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/hooks/useYjsProvider.ts`**
- Initializes `WebsocketProvider` from y-websocket
- Handles connection status and awareness

**However, comments are NOT synced via WebSocket.** The current implementation:
- Comments are fetched via REST API polling (every 10 seconds in `CommentSidebar.tsx`)
- Comments are stored/retrieved from GitHub files
- Real-time WebSocket sync is only used for document content (Yjs CRDT)

### 3. Frontend Comment Components

### 4. Comment Storage

**Storage Location:** GitHub repository in `.mume/` folder

Comments are stored as **YAML frontmatter files** directly in the GitHub repository:
- Storage path: `.mume/{documentPath}` (e.g., `.mume/README.md`, `.mume/docs/guide.md`)
- File format: YAML frontmatter + Markdown body

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/services/github.service.ts`** (lines 757-833)

Key methods:
- `getCommentFile()` - Fetches comment file from GitHub (returns null if not exists)
- `saveCommentFile()` - Creates or updates comment file in GitHub

**Example comment file structure:**
```yaml
---
version: 1
documentPath: README.md
comments:
  - id: c-abc123
    charStart: 0
    charEnd: 50
    author:
      username: johndoe
      avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/123
    text: This introduction could be clearer
    resolved: false
    createdAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    updatedAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    replies:
      - id: r-xyz789
        author:
          username: janedoe
          avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/456
        text: I agree, let me revise it
        createdAt: 2024-01-01T01:00:00.000Z
---

# Comments for README.md

This file contains review comments for the associated document.
Do not edit manually - managed by the collaborative editor.
```

**Note:** The archived SQL migrations (`003_create_comments_table.sql`, `004_create_comment_replies_table.sql`) indicate there was once a PostgreSQL-based approach, but the current implementation uses GitHub as the source of truth.

### 5. Real-Time Sync Mechanism

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/server.ts`**

The real-time sync uses **Yjs with WebSocket (y-websocket)**:
- WebSocket server runs on the same port as the HTTP server (default: 3000)
- Uses `y-websocket/bin/utils` for connection handling
- Document name is extracted from the WebSocket URL path

**Frontend hook: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/hooks/useYjsProvider.ts`**
- Initializes `WebsocketProvider` from y-websocket
- Handles connection status and awareness

**However, comments are NOT synced via WebSocket.** The current implementation:
- Comments are fetched via REST API polling (every 10 seconds in `CommentSidebar.tsx`)
- Comments are stored/retrieved from GitHub files
- Real-time WebSocket sync is only used for document content (Yjs CRDT)

### 4. Comment Storage

**Storage Location:** GitHub repository in `.mume/` folder

Comments are stored as **YAML frontmatter files** directly in the GitHub repository:
- Storage path: `.mume/{documentPath}` (e.g., `.mume/README.md`, `.mume/docs/guide.md`)
- File format: YAML frontmatter + Markdown body

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/services/github.service.ts`** (lines 757-833)

Key methods:
- `getCommentFile()` - Fetches comment file from GitHub (returns null if not exists)
- `saveCommentFile()` - Creates or updates comment file in GitHub

**Example comment file structure:**
```yaml
---
version: 1
documentPath: README.md
comments:
  - id: c-abc123
    charStart: 0
    charEnd: 50
    author:
      username: johndoe
      avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/123
    text: This introduction could be clearer
    resolved: false
    createdAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    updatedAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    replies:
      - id: r-xyz789
        author:
          username: janedoe
          avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/456
        text: I agree, let me revise it
        createdAt: 2024-01-01T01:00:00.000Z
---

# Comments for README.md

This file contains review comments for the associated document.
Do not edit manually - managed by the collaborative editor.
```

**Note:** The archived SQL migrations (`003_create_comments_table.sql`, `004_create_comment_replies_table.sql`) indicate there was once a PostgreSQL-based approach, but the current implementation uses GitHub as the source of truth.

### 5. Real-Time Sync Mechanism

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/server.ts`**

The real-time sync uses **Yjs with WebSocket (y-websocket)**:
- WebSocket server runs on the same port as the HTTP server (default: 3000)
- Uses `y-websocket/bin/utils` for connection handling
- Document name is extracted from the WebSocket URL path

**Frontend hook: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/hooks/useYjsProvider.ts`**
- Initializes `WebsocketProvider` from y-websocket
- Handles connection status and awareness

**However, comments are NOT synced via WebSocket.** The current implementation:
- Comments are fetched via REST API polling (every 10 seconds in `CommentSidebar.tsx`)
- Comments are stored/retrieved from GitHub files
- Real-time WebSocket sync is only used for document content (Yjs CRDT)

## Comment System Architecture Summary

### 1. Backend Comment Routes and Handlers

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/routes/comment.routes.ts`**

The comment API provides these endpoints:

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/comments` | POST | Create a new comment on a text range |
| `/api/comments/:commentId/replies` | POST | Add a reply to an existing comment |
| `/api/comments/:commentId` | PATCH | Update comment (resolve/unresolve) |
| `/api/comments/:commentId` | DELETE | Delete a comment (author only) |

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/routes/repository.routes.ts`** (lines 378-453)

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/repositories/:owner/:repo/comments` | GET | Fetch all comments for a document |

### 2. Comment Data Models/Types

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/services/comment-file.service.ts`**

```typescript
// Author information
interface CommentAuthor {
  username: string;
  avatarUrl: string | null;
}

// Reply to a comment (flat structure - no nested replies)
interface CommentReply {
  id: string;           // Generated with nanoid: "r-{id}"
  author: CommentAuthor;
  text: string;
  createdAt: string;
}

// Main comment entity
interface DocumentComment {
  id: string;           // Generated with nanoid: "c-{id}"
  charStart: number;    // Start character position in document
  charEnd: number;      // End character position in document
  author: CommentAuthor;
  text: string;
  resolved: boolean;
  createdAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
  replies: CommentReply[];  // Flat array of replies (NO parent_id)
}

// Comment file structure
interface CommentFileData {
  version: number;
  documentPath: string;
  comments: DocumentComment[];
}
```

**Key observation: There is NO `parent_id` or nested reply structure.** Replies are stored as a flat array within each comment. This is a single-level threading model (comments have replies, but replies cannot have sub-replies).

## Comment System Architecture Summary

### 1. Backend Comment Routes and Handlers

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/routes/comment.routes.ts`**

The comment API provides these endpoints:

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/comments` | POST | Create a new comment on a text range |
| `/api/comments/:commentId/replies` | POST | Add a reply to an existing comment |
| `/api/comments/:commentId` | PATCH | Update comment (resolve/unresolve) |
| `/api/comments/:commentId` | DELETE | Delete a comment (author only) |

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/routes/repository.routes.ts`** (lines 378-453)

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/repositories/:owner/:repo/comments` | GET | Fetch all comments for a document |

### 2. Comment Data Models/Types

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/services/comment-file.service.ts`**

```typescript
// Author information
interface CommentAuthor {
  username: string;
  avatarUrl: string | null;
}

// Reply to a comment (flat structure - no nested replies)
interface CommentReply {
  id: string;           // Generated with nanoid: "r-{id}"
  author: CommentAuthor;
  text: string;
  createdAt: string;
}

// Main comment entity
interface DocumentComment {
  id: string;           // Generated with nanoid: "c-{id}"
  charStart: number;    // Start character position in document
  charEnd: number;      // End character position in document
  author: CommentAuthor;
  text: string;
  resolved: boolean;
  createdAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
  replies: CommentReply[];  // Flat array of replies (NO parent_id)
}

// Comment file structure
interface CommentFileData {
  version: number;
  documentPath: string;
  comments: DocumentComment[];
}
```

**Key observation: There is NO `parent_id` or nested reply structure.** Replies are stored as a flat array within each comment. This is a single-level threading model (comments have replies, but replies cannot have sub-replies).

### 3. Frontend Comment Components

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/CommentSidebar.tsx`**
- Main sidebar panel showing all comments for a document
- Displays comment threads with author, timestamp, text
- Shows replies nested under each comment
- Provides Reply, Resolve/Unresolve, Delete actions
- Polls for updates every 10 seconds
- Filters by resolved/unresolved status

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/AddCommentModal.tsx`**
- Modal for creating new comments
- Shows selected text preview with character range
- Submits to `/api/comments` endpoint

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/CommentHighlights.tsx`**
- Renders visual highlights in the editor for commented text ranges
- Uses mirror-div technique for accurate positioning
- Supports active/resolved state styling
- Clickable to navigate to comment in sidebar

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/EditorLayout.tsx`** (integration)
- Coordinates comment components
- Manages comment state and sidebar visibility
- Handles bi-directional navigation (sidebar <-> editor highlights)

### 4. Comment Storage

**Storage Location:** GitHub repository in `.mume/` folder

Comments are stored as **YAML frontmatter files** directly in the GitHub repository:
- Storage path: `.mume/{documentPath}` (e.g., `.mume/README.md`, `.mume/docs/guide.md`)
- File format: YAML frontmatter + Markdown body

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/services/github.service.ts`** (lines 757-833)

Key methods:
- `getCommentFile()` - Fetches comment file from GitHub (returns null if not exists)
- `saveCommentFile()` - Creates or updates comment file in GitHub

**Example comment file structure:**
```yaml
---
version: 1
documentPath: README.md
comments:
  - id: c-abc123
    charStart: 0
    charEnd: 50
    author:
      username: johndoe
      avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/123
    text: This introduction could be clearer
    resolved: false
    createdAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    updatedAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    replies:
      - id: r-xyz789
        author:
          username: janedoe
          avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/456
        text: I agree, let me revise it
        createdAt: 2024-01-01T01:00:00.000Z
---

# Comments for README.md

This file contains review comments for the associated document.
Do not edit manually - managed by the collaborative editor.
```

**Note:** The archived SQL migrations (`003_create_comments_table.sql`, `004_create_comment_replies_table.sql`) indicate there was once a PostgreSQL-based approach, but the current implementation uses GitHub as the source of truth.

### 5. Real-Time Sync Mechanism

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/server.ts`**

The real-time sync uses **Yjs with WebSocket (y-websocket)**:
- WebSocket server runs on the same port as the HTTP server (default: 3000)
- Uses `y-websocket/bin/utils` for connection handling
- Document name is extracted from the WebSocket URL path

**Frontend hook: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/hooks/useYjsProvider.ts`**
- Initializes `WebsocketProvider` from y-websocket
- Handles connection status and awareness

**However, comments are NOT synced via WebSocket.** The current implementation:
- Comments are fetched via REST API polling (every 10 seconds in `CommentSidebar.tsx`)
- Comments are stored/retrieved from GitHub files
- Real-time WebSocket sync is only used for document content (Yjs CRDT)

### 4. Comment Storage

**Storage Location:** GitHub repository in `.mume/` folder

Comments are stored as **YAML frontmatter files** directly in the GitHub repository:
- Storage path: `.mume/{documentPath}` (e.g., `.mume/README.md`, `.mume/docs/guide.md`)
- File format: YAML frontmatter + Markdown body

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/services/github.service.ts`** (lines 757-833)

Key methods:
- `getCommentFile()` - Fetches comment file from GitHub (returns null if not exists)
- `saveCommentFile()` - Creates or updates comment file in GitHub

**Example comment file structure:**
```yaml
---
version: 1
documentPath: README.md
comments:
  - id: c-abc123
    charStart: 0
    charEnd: 50
    author:
      username: johndoe
      avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/123
    text: This introduction could be clearer
    resolved: false
    createdAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    updatedAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    replies:
      - id: r-xyz789
        author:
          username: janedoe
          avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/456
        text: I agree, let me revise it
        createdAt: 2024-01-01T01:00:00.000Z
---

# Comments for README.md

This file contains review comments for the associated document.
Do not edit manually - managed by the collaborative editor.
```

**Note:** The archived SQL migrations (`003_create_comments_table.sql`, `004_create_comment_replies_table.sql`) indicate there was once a PostgreSQL-based approach, but the current implementation uses GitHub as the source of truth.

### 5. Real-Time Sync Mechanism

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/server.ts`**

The real-time sync uses **Yjs with WebSocket (y-websocket)**:
- WebSocket server runs on the same port as the HTTP server (default: 3000)
- Uses `y-websocket/bin/utils` for connection handling
- Document name is extracted from the WebSocket URL path

**Frontend hook: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/hooks/useYjsProvider.ts`**
- Initializes `WebsocketProvider` from y-websocket
- Handles connection status and awareness

**However, comments are NOT synced via WebSocket.** The current implementation:
- Comments are fetched via REST API polling (every 10 seconds in `CommentSidebar.tsx`)
- Comments are stored/retrieved from GitHub files
- Real-time WebSocket sync is only used for document content (Yjs CRDT)

- `saveCommentFile()` - Creates or updates comment file in GitHub

**Example comment file structure:**
```yaml
---
version: 1
documentPath: README.md
comments:
  - id: c-abc123
    charStart: 0
    charEnd: 50
    author:
      username: johndoe
      avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/123
    text: This introduction could be clearer
    resolved: false
    createdAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    updatedAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    replies:
      - id: r-xyz789
        author:
          username: janedoe
          avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/456
        text: I agree, let me revise it
        createdAt: 2024-01-01T01:00:00.000Z
---

# Comments for README.md

This file contains review comments for the associated document.
Do not edit manually - managed by the collaborative editor.
```

**Note:** The archived SQL migrations (`003_create_comments_table.sql`, `004_create_comment_replies_table.sql`) indicate there was once a PostgreSQL-based approach, but the current implementation uses GitHub as the source of truth.

### 5. Real-Time Sync Mechanism

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/server.ts`**

The real-time sync uses **Yjs with WebSocket (y-websocket)**:
- WebSocket server runs on the same port as the HTTP server (default: 3000)
- Uses `y-websocket/bin/utils` for connection handling
- Document name is extracted from the WebSocket URL path

**Frontend hook: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/hooks/useYjsProvider.ts`**
- Initializes `WebsocketProvider` from y-websocket
- Handles connection status and awareness

**However, comments are NOT synced via WebSocket.** The current implementation:
- Comments are fetched via REST API polling (every 10 seconds in `CommentSidebar.tsx`)
- Comments are stored/retrieved from GitHub files
- Real-time WebSocket sync is only used for document content (Yjs CRDT)

### 2. Comment Data Models/Types

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/services/comment-file.service.ts`**

```typescript
// Author information
interface CommentAuthor {
  username: string;
  avatarUrl: string | null;
}

// Reply to a comment (flat structure - no nested replies)
interface CommentReply {
  id: string;           // Generated with nanoid: "r-{id}"
  author: CommentAuthor;
  text: string;
  createdAt: string;
}

// Main comment entity
interface DocumentComment {
  id: string;           // Generated with nanoid: "c-{id}"
  charStart: number;    // Start character position in document
  charEnd: number;      // End character position in document
  author: CommentAuthor;
  text: string;
  resolved: boolean;
  createdAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
  replies: CommentReply[];  // Flat array of replies (NO parent_id)
}

// Comment file structure
interface CommentFileData {
  version: number;
  documentPath: string;
  comments: DocumentComment[];
}
```

**Key observation: There is NO `parent_id` or nested reply structure.** Replies are stored as a flat array within each comment. This is a single-level threading model (comments have replies, but replies cannot have sub-replies).

## Comment System Architecture Summary

### 1. Backend Comment Routes and Handlers

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/routes/comment.routes.ts`**

The comment API provides these endpoints:

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/comments` | POST | Create a new comment on a text range |
| `/api/comments/:commentId/replies` | POST | Add a reply to an existing comment |
| `/api/comments/:commentId` | PATCH | Update comment (resolve/unresolve) |
| `/api/comments/:commentId` | DELETE | Delete a comment (author only) |

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/routes/repository.routes.ts`** (lines 378-453)

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/repositories/:owner/:repo/comments` | GET | Fetch all comments for a document |

### 2. Comment Data Models/Types

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/services/comment-file.service.ts`**

```typescript
// Author information
interface CommentAuthor {
  username: string;
  avatarUrl: string | null;
}

// Reply to a comment (flat structure - no nested replies)
interface CommentReply {
  id: string;           // Generated with nanoid: "r-{id}"
  author: CommentAuthor;
  text: string;
  createdAt: string;
}

// Main comment entity
interface DocumentComment {
  id: string;           // Generated with nanoid: "c-{id}"
  charStart: number;    // Start character position in document
  charEnd: number;      // End character position in document
  author: CommentAuthor;
  text: string;
  resolved: boolean;
  createdAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
  replies: CommentReply[];  // Flat array of replies (NO parent_id)
}

// Comment file structure
interface CommentFileData {
  version: number;
  documentPath: string;
  comments: DocumentComment[];
}
```

**Key observation: There is NO `parent_id` or nested reply structure.** Replies are stored as a flat array within each comment. This is a single-level threading model (comments have replies, but replies cannot have sub-replies).

### 3. Frontend Comment Components

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/CommentSidebar.tsx`**
- Main sidebar panel showing all comments for a document
- Displays comment threads with author, timestamp, text
- Shows replies nested under each comment
- Provides Reply, Resolve/Unresolve, Delete actions
- Polls for updates every 10 seconds
- Filters by resolved/unresolved status

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/AddCommentModal.tsx`**
- Modal for creating new comments
- Shows selected text preview with character range
- Submits to `/api/comments` endpoint

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/CommentHighlights.tsx`**
- Renders visual highlights in the editor for commented text ranges
- Uses mirror-div technique for accurate positioning
- Supports active/resolved state styling
- Clickable to navigate to comment in sidebar

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/EditorLayout.tsx`** (integration)
- Coordinates comment components
- Manages comment state and sidebar visibility
- Handles bi-directional navigation (sidebar <-> editor highlights)

### 4. Comment Storage

**Storage Location:** GitHub repository in `.mume/` folder

Comments are stored as **YAML frontmatter files** directly in the GitHub repository:
- Storage path: `.mume/{documentPath}` (e.g., `.mume/README.md`, `.mume/docs/guide.md`)
- File format: YAML frontmatter + Markdown body

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/services/github.service.ts`** (lines 757-833)

Key methods:
- `getCommentFile()` - Fetches comment file from GitHub (returns null if not exists)
- `saveCommentFile()` - Creates or updates comment file in GitHub

**Example comment file structure:**
```yaml
---
version: 1
documentPath: README.md
comments:
  - id: c-abc123
    charStart: 0
    charEnd: 50
    author:
      username: johndoe
      avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/123
    text: This introduction could be clearer
    resolved: false
    createdAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    updatedAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    replies:
      - id: r-xyz789
        author:
          username: janedoe
          avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/456
        text: I agree, let me revise it
        createdAt: 2024-01-01T01:00:00.000Z
---

# Comments for README.md

This file contains review comments for the associated document.
Do not edit manually - managed by the collaborative editor.
```

**Note:** The archived SQL migrations (`003_create_comments_table.sql`, `004_create_comment_replies_table.sql`) indicate there was once a PostgreSQL-based approach, but the current implementation uses GitHub as the source of truth.

### 5. Real-Time Sync Mechanism

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/server.ts`**

The real-time sync uses **Yjs with WebSocket (y-websocket)**:
- WebSocket server runs on the same port as the HTTP server (default: 3000)
- Uses `y-websocket/bin/utils` for connection handling
- Document name is extracted from the WebSocket URL path

**Frontend hook: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/hooks/useYjsProvider.ts`**
- Initializes `WebsocketProvider` from y-websocket
- Handles connection status and awareness

**However, comments are NOT synced via WebSocket.** The current implementation:
- Comments are fetched via REST API polling (every 10 seconds in `CommentSidebar.tsx`)
- Comments are stored/retrieved from GitHub files
- Real-time WebSocket sync is only used for document content (Yjs CRDT)

```typescript
  author: CommentAuthor;
  text: string;
  createdAt: string;
}

// Main comment entity
interface DocumentComment {
  id: string;           // Generated with nanoid: "c-{id}"
  charStart: number;    // Start character position in document
  charEnd: number;      // End character position in document
  author: CommentAuthor;
  text: string;
  resolved: boolean;
  createdAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
  replies: CommentReply[];  // Flat array of replies (NO parent_id)
}

// Comment file structure
interface CommentFileData {
  version: number;
  documentPath: string;
  comments: DocumentComment[];
}
```

**Key observation: There is NO `parent_id` or nested reply structure.** Replies are stored as a flat array within each comment. This is a single-level threading model (comments have replies, but replies cannot have sub-replies).

### 3. Frontend Comment Components

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/CommentSidebar.tsx`**
- Main sidebar panel showing all comments for a document
- Displays comment threads with author, timestamp, text
- Shows replies nested under each comment
- Provides Reply, Resolve/Unresolve, Delete actions
- Polls for updates every 10 seconds
- Filters by resolved/unresolved status

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/AddCommentModal.tsx`**
- Modal for creating new comments
- Shows selected text preview with character range
- Submits to `/api/comments` endpoint

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/CommentHighlights.tsx`**
- Renders visual highlights in the editor for commented text ranges
- Uses mirror-div technique for accurate positioning
- Supports active/resolved state styling
- Clickable to navigate to comment in sidebar

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/EditorLayout.tsx`** (integration)
- Coordinates comment components
- Manages comment state and sidebar visibility
- Handles bi-directional navigation (sidebar <-> editor highlights)

### 4. Comment Storage

**Storage Location:** GitHub repository in `.mume/` folder

Comments are stored as **YAML frontmatter files** directly in the GitHub repository:
- Storage path: `.mume/{documentPath}` (e.g., `.mume/README.md`, `.mume/docs/guide.md`)
- File format: YAML frontmatter + Markdown body

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/services/github.service.ts`** (lines 757-833)

Key methods:
- `getCommentFile()` - Fetches comment file from GitHub (returns null if not exists)
- `saveCommentFile()` - Creates or updates comment file in GitHub

**Example comment file structure:**
```yaml
---
version: 1
documentPath: README.md
comments:
  - id: c-abc123
    charStart: 0
    charEnd: 50
    author:
      username: johndoe
      avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/123
    text: This introduction could be clearer
    resolved: false
    createdAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    updatedAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    replies:
      - id: r-xyz789
        author:
          username: janedoe
          avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/456
        text: I agree, let me revise it
        createdAt: 2024-01-01T01:00:00.000Z
---

# Comments for README.md

This file contains review comments for the associated document.
Do not edit manually - managed by the collaborative editor.
```

**Note:** The archived SQL migrations (`003_create_comments_table.sql`, `004_create_comment_replies_table.sql`) indicate there was once a PostgreSQL-based approach, but the current implementation uses GitHub as the source of truth.

### 5. Real-Time Sync Mechanism

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/server.ts`**

The real-time sync uses **Yjs with WebSocket (y-websocket)**:
- WebSocket server runs on the same port as the HTTP server (default: 3000)
- Uses `y-websocket/bin/utils` for connection handling
- Document name is extracted from the WebSocket URL path

**Frontend hook: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/hooks/useYjsProvider.ts`**
- Initializes `WebsocketProvider` from y-websocket
- Handles connection status and awareness

**However, comments are NOT synced via WebSocket.** The current implementation:
- Comments are fetched via REST API polling (every 10 seconds in `CommentSidebar.tsx`)
- Comments are stored/retrieved from GitHub files
- Real-time WebSocket sync is only used for document content (Yjs CRDT)

```yaml
  - id: c-abc123
    charStart: 0
    charEnd: 50
    author:
      username: johndoe
      avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/123
    text: This introduction could be clearer
    resolved: false
    createdAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    updatedAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    replies:
      - id: r-xyz789
        author:
          username: janedoe
          avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/456
        text: I agree, let me revise it
        createdAt: 2024-01-01T01:00:00.000Z
---

# Comments for README.md

This file contains review comments for the associated document.
Do not edit manually - managed by the collaborative editor.
```

**Note:** The archived SQL migrations (`003_create_comments_table.sql`, `004_create_comment_replies_table.sql`) indicate there was once a PostgreSQL-based approach, but the current implementation uses GitHub as the source of truth.

### 5. Real-Time Sync Mechanism

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/server.ts`**

The real-time sync uses **Yjs with WebSocket (y-websocket)**:
- WebSocket server runs on the same port as the HTTP server (default: 3000)
- Uses `y-websocket/bin/utils` for connection handling
- Document name is extracted from the WebSocket URL path

**Frontend hook: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/hooks/useYjsProvider.ts`**
- Initializes `WebsocketProvider` from y-websocket
- Handles connection status and awareness

**However, comments are NOT synced via WebSocket.** The current implementation:
- Comments are fetched via REST API polling (every 10 seconds in `CommentSidebar.tsx`)
- Comments are stored/retrieved from GitHub files
- Real-time WebSocket sync is only used for document content (Yjs CRDT)

### Key Architectural Points

1. **No parent_id for replies** - Replies are flat arrays within comments, not hierarchical
2. **GitHub as storage** - Comments persisted as YAML files in `.mume/` folder
3. **Polling for updates** - No real-time sync for comments (10-second polling)
4. **Character-based positioning** - Comments reference `charStart`/`charEnd` character positions
5. **User-based deletion** - Only comment authors can delete

## Comment System Architecture Summary

### 1. Backend Comment Routes and Handlers

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/routes/comment.routes.ts`**

The comment API provides these endpoints:

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/comments` | POST | Create a new comment on a text range |
| `/api/comments/:commentId/replies` | POST | Add a reply to an existing comment |
| `/api/comments/:commentId` | PATCH | Update comment (resolve/unresolve) |
| `/api/comments/:commentId` | DELETE | Delete a comment (author only) |

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/routes/repository.routes.ts`** (lines 378-453)

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/repositories/:owner/:repo/comments` | GET | Fetch all comments for a document |

### 2. Comment Data Models/Types

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/services/comment-file.service.ts`**

```typescript
// Author information
interface CommentAuthor {
  username: string;
  avatarUrl: string | null;
}

// Reply to a comment (flat structure - no nested replies)
interface CommentReply {
  id: string;           // Generated with nanoid: "r-{id}"
  author: CommentAuthor;
  text: string;
  createdAt: string;
}

// Main comment entity
interface DocumentComment {
  id: string;           // Generated with nanoid: "c-{id}"
  charStart: number;    // Start character position in document
  charEnd: number;      // End character position in document
  author: CommentAuthor;
  text: string;
  resolved: boolean;
  createdAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
  replies: CommentReply[];  // Flat array of replies (NO parent_id)
}

// Comment file structure
interface CommentFileData {
  version: number;
  documentPath: string;
  comments: DocumentComment[];
}
```

**Key observation: There is NO `parent_id` or nested reply structure.** Replies are stored as a flat array within each comment. This is a single-level threading model (comments have replies, but replies cannot have sub-replies).

### 3. Frontend Comment Components

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/CommentSidebar.tsx`**
- Main sidebar panel showing all comments for a document
- Displays comment threads with author, timestamp, text
- Shows replies nested under each comment
- Provides Reply, Resolve/Unresolve, Delete actions
- Polls for updates every 10 seconds
- Filters by resolved/unresolved status

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/AddCommentModal.tsx`**
- Modal for creating new comments
- Shows selected text preview with character range
- Submits to `/api/comments` endpoint

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/CommentHighlights.tsx`**
- Renders visual highlights in the editor for commented text ranges
- Uses mirror-div technique for accurate positioning
- Supports active/resolved state styling
- Clickable to navigate to comment in sidebar

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/EditorLayout.tsx`** (integration)
- Coordinates comment components
- Manages comment state and sidebar visibility
- Handles bi-directional navigation (sidebar <-> editor highlights)

### 4. Comment Storage

**Storage Location:** GitHub repository in `.mume/` folder

Comments are stored as **YAML frontmatter files** directly in the GitHub repository:
- Storage path: `.mume/{documentPath}` (e.g., `.mume/README.md`, `.mume/docs/guide.md`)
- File format: YAML frontmatter + Markdown body

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/services/github.service.ts`** (lines 757-833)

Key methods:
- `getCommentFile()` - Fetches comment file from GitHub (returns null if not exists)
- `saveCommentFile()` - Creates or updates comment file in GitHub

**Example comment file structure:**
```yaml
---
version: 1
documentPath: README.md
comments:
  - id: c-abc123
    charStart: 0
    charEnd: 50
    author:
      username: johndoe
      avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/123
    text: This introduction could be clearer
    resolved: false
    createdAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    updatedAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    replies:
      - id: r-xyz789
        author:
          username: janedoe
          avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/456
        text: I agree, let me revise it
        createdAt: 2024-01-01T01:00:00.000Z
---

# Comments for README.md

This file contains review comments for the associated document.
Do not edit manually - managed by the collaborative editor.
```

**Note:** The archived SQL migrations (`003_create_comments_table.sql`, `004_create_comment_replies_table.sql`) indicate there was once a PostgreSQL-based approach, but the current implementation uses GitHub as the source of truth.

### 5. Real-Time Sync Mechanism

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/server.ts`**

## Comment System Architecture Summary

### 1. Backend Comment Routes and Handlers

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/routes/comment.routes.ts`**

The comment API provides these endpoints:

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/comments` | POST | Create a new comment on a text range |
| `/api/comments/:commentId/replies` | POST | Add a reply to an existing comment |
| `/api/comments/:commentId` | PATCH | Update comment (resolve/unresolve) |
| `/api/comments/:commentId` | DELETE | Delete a comment (author only) |

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/routes/repository.routes.ts`** (lines 378-453)

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/repositories/:owner/:repo/comments` | GET | Fetch all comments for a document |

### 2. Comment Data Models/Types

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/services/comment-file.service.ts`**

```typescript
// Author information
interface CommentAuthor {
  username: string;
  avatarUrl: string | null;
}

// Reply to a comment (flat structure - no nested replies)
interface CommentReply {
  id: string;           // Generated with nanoid: "r-{id}"
  author: CommentAuthor;
  text: string;
  createdAt: string;
}

// Main comment entity
interface DocumentComment {
  id: string;           // Generated with nanoid: "c-{id}"
  charStart: number;    // Start character position in document
  charEnd: number;      // End character position in document
  author: CommentAuthor;
  text: string;
  resolved: boolean;
  createdAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
  replies: CommentReply[];  // Flat array of replies (NO parent_id)
}

// Comment file structure
interface CommentFileData {
  version: number;
  documentPath: string;
  comments: DocumentComment[];
}
```

**Key observation: There is NO `parent_id` or nested reply structure.** Replies are stored as a flat array within each comment. This is a single-level threading model (comments have replies, but replies cannot have sub-replies).

### 3. Frontend Comment Components

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/CommentSidebar.tsx`**
- Main sidebar panel showing all comments for a document
- Displays comment threads with author, timestamp, text
- Shows replies nested under each comment
- Provides Reply, Resolve/Unresolve, Delete actions
- Polls for updates every 10 seconds
- Filters by resolved/unresolved status

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/AddCommentModal.tsx`**
- Modal for creating new comments
- Shows selected text preview with character range
- Submits to `/api/comments` endpoint

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/CommentHighlights.tsx`**
- Renders visual highlights in the editor for commented text ranges
- Uses mirror-div technique for accurate positioning
- Supports active/resolved state styling
- Clickable to navigate to comment in sidebar

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/components/EditorLayout.tsx`** (integration)
- Coordinates comment components
- Manages comment state and sidebar visibility
- Handles bi-directional navigation (sidebar <-> editor highlights)

### 4. Comment Storage

**Storage Location:** GitHub repository in `.mume/` folder

Comments are stored as **YAML frontmatter files** directly in the GitHub repository:
- Storage path: `.mume/{documentPath}` (e.g., `.mume/README.md`, `.mume/docs/guide.md`)
- File format: YAML frontmatter + Markdown body

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/services/github.service.ts`** (lines 757-833)

Key methods:
- `getCommentFile()` - Fetches comment file from GitHub (returns null if not exists)
- `saveCommentFile()` - Creates or updates comment file in GitHub

**Example comment file structure:**
```yaml
---
version: 1
documentPath: README.md
comments:
  - id: c-abc123
    charStart: 0
    charEnd: 50
    author:
      username: johndoe
      avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/123
    text: This introduction could be clearer
    resolved: false
    createdAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    updatedAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    replies:
      - id: r-xyz789
        author:
          username: janedoe
          avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/456
        text: I agree, let me revise it
        createdAt: 2024-01-01T01:00:00.000Z
---

# Comments for README.md

This file contains review comments for the associated document.
Do not edit manually - managed by the collaborative editor.
```

**Note:** The archived SQL migrations (`003_create_comments_table.sql`, `004_create_comment_replies_table.sql`) indicate there was once a PostgreSQL-based approach, but the current implementation uses GitHub as the source of truth.

### 5. Real-Time Sync Mechanism

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/server.ts`**

The real-time sync uses **Yjs with WebSocket (y-websocket)**:
- WebSocket server runs on the same port as the HTTP server (default: 3000)
- Uses `y-websocket/bin/utils` for connection handling
- Document name is extracted from the WebSocket URL path

**Frontend hook: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/hooks/useYjsProvider.ts`**
- Initializes `WebsocketProvider` from y-websocket
- Handles connection status and awareness

**However, comments are NOT synced via WebSocket.** The current implementation:
- Comments are fetched via REST API polling (every 10 seconds in `CommentSidebar.tsx`)
- Comments are stored/retrieved from GitHub files
- Real-time WebSocket sync is only used for document content (Yjs CRDT)

### 2. Comment Data Models/Types

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/services/comment-file.service.ts`**

```typescript
// Author information
interface CommentAuthor {
  username: string;
  avatarUrl: string | null;
}

// Reply to a comment (flat structure - no nested replies)
interface CommentReply {
  id: string;           // Generated with nanoid: "r-{id}"
  author: CommentAuthor;
```

### 4. Comment Storage

**Storage Location:** GitHub repository in `.mume/` folder

Comments are stored as **YAML frontmatter files** directly in the GitHub repository:
- Storage path: `.mume/{documentPath}` (e.g., `.mume/README.md`, `.mume/docs/guide.md`)
- File format: YAML frontmatter + Markdown body

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/services/github.service.ts`** (lines 757-833)

Key methods:
- `getCommentFile()` - Fetches comment file from GitHub (returns null if not exists)
- `saveCommentFile()` - Creates or updates comment file in GitHub

**Example comment file structure:**
```yaml
---
version: 1
documentPath: README.md
comments:
  - id: c-abc123
    charStart: 0
    charEnd: 50
    author:
      username: johndoe
      avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/123
    text: This introduction could be clearer
    resolved: false
    createdAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    updatedAt: 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z
    replies:
      - id: r-xyz789
        author:
          username: janedoe
          avatarUrl: https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/456
        text: I agree, let me revise it
        createdAt: 2024-01-01T01:00:00.000Z
---

# Comments for README.md

This file contains review comments for the associated document.
Do not edit manually - managed by the collaborative editor.
```

**Note:** The archived SQL migrations (`003_create_comments_table.sql`, `004_create_comment_replies_table.sql`) indicate there was once a PostgreSQL-based approach, but the current implementation uses GitHub as the source of truth.

### 5. Real-Time Sync Mechanism

**File: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/api/src/server.ts`**

The real-time sync uses **Yjs with WebSocket (y-websocket)**:
- WebSocket server runs on the same port as the HTTP server (default: 3000)
- Uses `y-websocket/bin/utils` for connection handling
- Document name is extracted from the WebSocket URL path

**Frontend hook: `/Users/leewsimpson/Github/mume/apps/frontend/src/hooks/useYjsProvider.ts`**
- Initializes `WebsocketProvider` from y-websocket
- Handles connection status and awareness

**However, comments are NOT synced via WebSocket.** The current implementation:
- Comments are fetched via REST API polling (every 10 seconds in `CommentSidebar.tsx`)
- Comments are stored/retrieved from GitHub files
- Real-time WebSocket sync is only used for document content (Yjs CRDT)

### Key Architectural Points

1. **No parent_id for replies** - Replies are flat arrays within comments, not hierarchical
2. **GitHub as storage** - Comments persisted as YAML files in `.mume/` folder
3. **Polling for updates** - No real-time sync for comments (10-second polling)
4. **Character-based positioning** - Comments reference `charStart`/`charEnd` character positions
5. **User-based deletion** - Only comment authors can delete their own comments
6. **Resolve/unresolve** - Any user can toggle resolved status

00051| /**
00052|  * Format timestamp as relative time (e.g., "2 hours ago")
00053|  */
00054| function formatRelativeTime(timestamp: string): string {
00055|   const now = new Date();
00056|   const date = new Date(timestamp);
00057|   const diffMs = now.getTime() - date.getTime();
00058|   const diffSeconds = Math.floor(diffMs / 1000);
00059|   const diffMinutes = Math.floor(diffSeconds / 60);
00060|   const diffHours = Math.floor(diffMinutes / 60);
00061|   const diffDays = Math.floor(diffHours / 24);
00062| 
00063|   if (diffSeconds < 60) {
00064|     return 'just now';
00065|   } else if (diffMinutes < 60) {
00066|     return `${diffMinutes} minute${diffMinutes !== 1 ? 's' : ''} ago`;
00067|   } else if (diffHours < 24) {
00068|     return `${diffHours} hour${diffHours !== 1 ? 's' : ''} ago`;
00069|   } else if (diffDays < 7) {
00070|     return `${diffDays} day${diffDays !== 1 ? 's' : ''} ago`;
00071|   } else {
00072|     return date.toLocaleDateString();
00073|   }
00074| }

00076| /**
00077|  * CommentSidebar component displays all comments for a document in a slide-in panel
00078|  */
00079| export function CommentSidebar({
00080|   isOpen,
00081|   onClose,
00082|   owner,
00083|   repo,
00084|   filePath,
00085|   currentUserId,
00086|   onCommentClick,
00087|   showResolved: showResolvedProp,
00088|   onShowResolvedChange,
00089| }: CommentSidebarProps) {
00090|   const [comments, setComments] = useState<Comment[]>([]);
00091|   const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
00092|   const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
00093|   const [showResolvedInternal, setShowResolvedInternal] = useState(false);
00094|   const [replyingTo, setReplyingTo] = useState<number | null>(null);
00095|   const [replyText, setReplyText] = useState('');
00096|   const [deletingCommentId, setDeletingCommentId] = useState<number | null>(null);
00097|   const [deleteConfirmCommentId, setDeleteConfirmCommentId] = useState<number | null>(null);
00098| 
00099|   // Use controlled or uncontrolled mode for showResolved
00100|   const showResolved = showResolvedProp ?? showResolvedInternal;
00101|   const setShowResolved = (value: boolean) => {
00102|     if (onShowResolvedChange) {
00103|       onShowResolvedChange(value);
00104|     } else {
00105|       setShowResolvedInternal(value);
00106|     }
00107|   };
00108| 
00109|   // Fetch comments from backend
00110|   const fetchComments = async () => {
00111|     try {
00112|       setLoading(true);
00113|       setError(null);
00114| 
00115|       const response = await fetch(
00116|         `${API_URL}/api/repositories/${owner}/${repo}/comments?filePath=${encodeURIComponent(filePath)}`,
00117|         {
00118|           credentials: 'include',
00119|         }
00120|       );
00121| 
00122|       if (!response.ok) {
00123|         throw new Error(`Failed to fetch comments: ${response.statusText}`);
00124|       }
00125| 
00126|       const data = await response.json();
00127|       setComments(data);
00128|     } catch (err) {
00129|       setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to fetch comments');
00130|     } finally {
00131|       setLoading(false);
00132|     }
00133|   };
00134| 
00135|   // Fetch comments on mount and when path changes
00136|   useEffect(() => {
00137|     if (isOpen) {
00138|       fetchComments();
00139|     }
00140|   }, [isOpen, owner, repo, filePath]);
00141| 
00142|   // Poll for updates every 10 seconds
00143|   useEffect(() => {
00144|     if (!isOpen) return;
00145| 
00146|     const interval = setInterval(() => {
00147|       fetchComments();
00148|     }, 10000); // 10 seconds
00149| 
00150|     return () => clearInterval(interval);
00151|   }, [isOpen, owner, repo, filePath]);
00152| 
00153|   const handleCommentClick = (comment: Comment) => {
00154|     if (onCommentClick) {
00155|       onCommentClick(comment);
00156|     }
00157|   };
00158| 
00159|   const handleReplySubmit = async (commentId: number) => {
00160|     if (!replyText.trim()) return;
00161| 
00162|     try {
00163|       const response = await fetch(
00164|         `${API_URL}/api/comments/${commentId}/replies`,
00165|         {
00166|           method: 'POST',
00167|           headers: {
00168|             'Content-Type': 'application/json',
00169|           },
00170|           credentials: 'include',
00171|           body: JSON.stringify({ text: replyText }),
00172|         }
00173|       );
00174| 
00175|       if (!response.ok) {
00176|         throw new Error('Failed to submit reply');
00177|       }
00178| 
00179|       // Reset reply state
00180|       setReplyText('');
00181|       setReplyingTo(null);
00182| 
00183|       // Refresh comments
00184|       await fetchComments();
00185|     } catch (err) {
00186|       setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to submit reply');
00187|     }
00188|   };
00189| 
00190|   const handleResolveToggle = async (commentId: number, currentResolved: boolean) => {
00191|     try {
00192|       const response = await fetch(
00193|         `${API_URL}/api/comments/${commentId}`,
00194|         {
00195|           method: 'PATCH',
00196|           headers: {
00197|             'Content-Type': 'application/json',
00198|           },
00199|           credentials: 'include',
00200|           body: JSON.stringify({ resolved: !currentResolved }),
00201|         }
00202|       );
00203| 
00204|       if (!response.ok) {
00205|         throw new Error('Failed to update comment');
00206|       }
00207| 
00208|       // Refresh comments
00209|       await fetchComments();
00210|     } catch (err) {
00211|       setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to update comment');
00212|     }
00213|   };
00214| 
00215|   const handleDeleteClick = (commentId: number) => {
00216|     setDeleteConfirmCommentId(commentId);
00217|   };
00218| 
00219|   const handleConfirmDelete = async () => {
00220|     if (!deleteConfirmCommentId) return;
00221| 
00222|     try {
00223|       setDeletingCommentId(deleteConfirmCommentId);
00224|       const response = await fetch(
00225|         `${API_URL}/api/comments/${deleteConfirmCommentId}`,
00226|         {
00227|           method: 'DELETE',
00228|           credentials: 'include',
00229|         }
00230|       );
00231| 
00232|       if (!response.ok) {
00233|         const errorData = await response.json();
00234|         throw new Error(errorData.error || 'Failed to delete comment');
00235|       }
00236| 
00237|       // Refresh comments
00238|       await fetchComments();
00239|       setDeletingCommentId(null);
00240|       setDeleteConfirmCommentId(null);
00241|     } catch (err) {
00242|       setDeletingCommentId(null);
00243|       setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to delete comment');
00244|     }
00245|   };
00246| 
00247|   const handleCancelDelete = () => {
00248|     setDeleteConfirmCommentId(null);
00249|   };
00250| 
00251|   // Filter comments based on resolved status visibility
00252|   const filteredComments = showResolved
00253|     ? comments
00254|     : comments.filter((c) => !c.resolved);
00255| 
00256|   if (!isOpen) return null;
00257| 
00258|   return (
00259|     <div className="comment-sidebar-overlay">
00260|       {/* Clickable background overlay to close sidebar */}
00261|       <div 
00262|         className="comment-sidebar-backdrop"
00263|         onClick={onClose}
00264|         aria-label="Close sidebar"
00265|       />
00266|       {/* Sidebar panel */}
00267|       <div className="comment-sidebar" data-testid="comment-sidebar">
00268|         <div className="comment-sidebar-header">
00269|           <div className="header-top">
00270|             <h2>Comments</h2>
00271|             <button className="close-button" onClick={onClose}>
00272|               ✕
00273|             </button>
00274|           </div>
00275|           <div className="header-controls">
00276|             <button
00277|               className="toggle-resolved-button"
00278|               onClick={() => setShowResolved(!showResolved)}
00279|             >
00280|               {showResolved ? 'Hide' : 'Show'} resolved
00281|             </button>
00282|           </div>
00283|         </div>
00284| 
00285|         <div className="comment-sidebar-content">
00286|           {loading && comments.length === 0 && (
00287|             <div className="empty-state">Loading comments...</div>
00288|           )}
00289| 
00290|           {error && (
00291|             <div className="error-state">
00292|               <p>{error}</p>
00293|               <button onClick={fetchComments} className="retry-button">
00294|                 Retry
00295|               </button>
00296|             </div>
00297|           )}
00298| 
00299|           {!loading && !error && comments.length === 0 && (
00300|             <div className="empty-state">
00301|               <p>No comments yet.</p>
00302|               <p className="empty-state-hint">
00303|                 Select text in the editor to add a comment.
00304|               </p>
00305|             </div>
00306|           )}
00307| 
00308|           {filteredComments.length > 0 && (
00309|             <div className="comments-list">
00310|               {filteredComments.map((comment) => (
00311|                 <div
00312|                   key={comment.id}
00313|                   className={`comment-thread ${comment.resolved ? 'resolved' : ''}`}
00314|                   data-comment-id={comment.id}
00315|                   data-testid="comment-item"
00316|                 >
00317|                   <div className="comment-thread-header">
00318|                     <div className="comment-header">
00319|                       <img
00320|                         src={comment.user.avatarUrl}

00330|                         </span>

00340|                           e.stopPropagation();

00343|                       >

00347|                         <button
00348|                           className="delete-button"
00349|                           onClick={(e) => {
00350|                             e.stopPropagation();

00354|                           title="Delete comment"

00358|                         </button>

00360|                     </div>
00361|                   </div>
00362|                   <div
00363|                     className="comment-body"
00364|                     onClick={() => handleCommentClick(comment)}

00047| /**
00048|  * Service for managing comments stored in GitHub as YAML frontmatter files
00049|  */
00050| export class CommentFileService {
00051|   /**
00052|    * Get the comment file path for a given document
00053|    * Comments are stored in a .mume folder at the repo root, preserving the original path structure.
00054|    * 
00055|    * Example: "README.md" → ".mume/README.md"
00056|    * Example: "docs/guide.md" → ".mume/docs/guide.md"
00057|    * Example: "folder/subfolder/file.md" → ".mume/folder/subfolder/file.md"
00058|    */
00059|   getCommentsFilePath(documentPath: string): string {
00060|     return `.mume/${documentPath}`;
00061|   }
00062| 
00063|   /**
00064|    * Parse comment file content
00065|    * Expects YAML frontmatter followed by markdown body
00066|    */
00067|   parseCommentFile(content: string, logger?: Logger): CommentFileData {
00068|     try {
00069|       // Extract YAML frontmatter
00070|       const frontmatterMatch = content.match(/^---\n([\s\S]*?)\n---/);
00071|       
00072|       if (!frontmatterMatch) {
00073|         throw new Error('Invalid comment file format: missing YAML frontmatter');
00074|       }
00075| 
00076|       const yamlContent = frontmatterMatch[1]!;
00077|       const data = yaml.load(yamlContent) as CommentFileData;
00078| 
00079|       // Validate structure
00080|       if (!data.version || !data.documentPath || !Array.isArray(data.comments)) {
00081|         throw new Error('Invalid comment file structure');
00082|       }
00083| 
00084|       return data;
00085|     } catch (error) {
00086|       logger?.error(
00087|         'Failed to parse comment file',
00088|         error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error)),
00089|         { operation: 'parseCommentFile' }
00090|       );
00091|       throw error;
00092|     }
00093|   }
00094| 
00095|   /**
00096|    * Serialize comment data to file format (YAML frontmatter + Markdown body)
00097|    */
00098|   serializeCommentFile(data: CommentFileData): string {
00099|     const yamlStr = yaml.dump(data, {
00100|       indent: 2,
00101|       lineWidth: -1, // No line wrapping
00102|       noRefs: true,
00103|     });
00104| 
00105|     const markdown = `---
00106| ${yamlStr}---
00107| 
00108| # Comments for ${data.documentPath}
00109| 
00110| This file contains review comments for the associated document.
00111| Do not edit manually - managed by the collaborative editor.
00112| `;
00113| 
00114|     return markdown;
00115|   }
00116| 
00117|   /**

00119|    */

00123|       documentPath,
00124|       comments: [],
00125|     };

00142|   /**
00143|    * Add a new comment to the comment data
00144|    */
00145|   addComment(
00146|     data: CommentFileData,
00147|     comment: Omit<DocumentComment, 'id' | 'createdAt' | 'updatedAt' | 'replies'>
00148|   ): { data: CommentFileData; commentId: string } {
00149|     const now = new Date().toISOString();
00150|     const commentId = this.generateCommentId();
00151| 
00152|     const newComment: DocumentComment = {
00153|       id: commentId,
00154|       charStart: comment.charStart,
00155|       charEnd: comment.charEnd,
00156|       author: comment.author,
00157|       text: comment.text,
00158|       resolved: comment.resolved,
00159|       createdAt: now,
00160|       updatedAt: now,
00161|       replies: [],
00162|     };
00163| 
00164|     data.comments.push(newComment);
00165| 
00166|     // Sort comments by charStart
00167|     data.comments.sort((a, b) => a.charStart - b.charStart);
00168| 
00169|     return { data, commentId };
00170|   }
00171| 
00172|   /**
00173|    * Add a reply to an existing comment
00174|    */
00175|   addReply(
00176|     data: CommentFileData,
00177|     commentId: string,
00178|     reply: Omit<CommentReply, 'id' | 'createdAt'>
00179|   ): { data: CommentFileData; replyId: string } {

00181|

00643|         }

00645|       
00646|       await route.fulfill({
00647|         status: 404,
00648|         contentType: 'application/json',
00649|         body: JSON.stringify({ error: 'Comment not found' }),
00650|       });
00651|     } else {
00652|       await route.continue();
00653|     }
00654|   });
00655| 
00656|   // Mock comment PATCH (resolve/unresolve)
00657|   await page.route(`${apiBaseUrl}/api/comments/*`, async (route: Route) => {
00658|     const method = route.request().method();
00659|     const url = route.request().url();
00660|     
00661|     // Skip if this is the replies endpoint
00662|     if (url.includes('/replies')) {
00663|       await route.continue();
00664|       return;
00665|     }
00666|     
00667|     if (method === 'PATCH') {
00668|       const commentIdMatch = url.match(/\/api\/comments\/([^/?]+)/);
00669|       const commentId = commentIdMatch?.[1];
00670|       
00671|       const body = route.request().postDataJSON();

00673|       
00674|       const commentData = mockComments.get(documentPath);

00680|

00688|               charEnd: comment.charEnd,
00689|               text: comment.text,
00690|               resolved: comment.resolved,
00691|               createdAt: comment.createdAt,
00692|               updatedAt: comment.updatedAt,
00693|               userId: 1,
00694|               user: {
00695|                 id: 1,
00696|                 username: comment.author.username,
00697|                 avatarUrl: comment.author.avatarUrl,
00698|               },
00699|               replies: comment.replies,
00700|             }),
00701|           });
00702|           return;
00703|         }
00704|       }
00705|       
00706|       await route.fulfill({
00707|         status: 404,
00708|         contentType: 'application/json',
00709|         body: JSON.stringify({ error: 'Comment not found' }),
00710|       });
00711|     } else if (method === 'DELETE') {
00712|       const commentIdMatch = url.match(/\/api\/comments\/([^/?]+)/);
00713|       const commentId = commentIdMatch?.[1];
00714|       
00715|       const urlObj = new URL(url);
00716|       const documentPath = urlObj.searchParams.get('documentPath') || '';
00717|       
00718|       const commentData = mockComments.get(documentPath);
00719|       if (commentData) {

00721|         if (index !== -1) {

00723|

00725|             status: 200,

00749|   const apiBaseUrl = 'http://localhost:3000';

00799|     const method = route.request().method();
00800| 
00801|     // Extract file path from URL
00802|     const match = url.match(/\/files\/(.+)$/);
00803|     const filePath = match?.[1] ? decodeURIComponent(match[1]) : '';
00804| 
00805|     if (method === 'GET') {
00806|       // Check if file was updated
00807|       const updated = fileUpdates.get(filePath);
00808|       if (updated) {

00811|           contentType: 'application/json',

00815|           }),
00816|         });
00817|         return;
00818|       }
00819| 
00820|       // Check if file was created
00821|       const created = createdFiles.get(filePath);
00822|       if (created) {
00823|         await route.fulfill({
00824|           status: 200,
00825|           contentType: 'application/json',
00826|           body: JSON.stringify({
00827|             content: created.content,
00828|             sha: created.sha,
00829|           }),
00830|         });
00831|         return;
00832|       }
00833| 
00834|       // Return mock file content
00835|       const file = TEST_FILES[filePath];
00836|       if (file) {
00837|         await route.fulfill({
00838|           status: 200,
00839|           contentType: 'application/json',
00840|           body: JSON.stringify({
00841|             content: file.content,
00842|             sha: file.sha,
00843|           }),
00844|         });
00845|       } else if (filePath.startsWith('test-') && filePath.endsWith('.md')) {
00846|         // Handle dynamic test files - return default content for test isolation

00848|           status: 200,
00849|           contentType: 'application/json',
00850|           body: JSON.stringify({
00851|             content: `# Test Document\n\nThis is a test document for E2E testing.\n`,
00852|             sha: `sha-test-${Date.now()}`,
00853|           }),
00854|         });
00855|       } else if (filePath.startsWith('docs/test-') && filePath.endsWith('.md')) {
00856|         // Handle dynamic nested test files
00857|         await route.fulfill({
00858|           status: 200,
00859|           contentType: 'application/json',
00860|           body: JSON.stringify({
00861|             content: `# Nested Test Document\n\nThis is a nested test document for E2E testing.\n`,
00862|             sha: `sha-nested-test-${Date.now()}`,
00863|           }),
00864|         });
00865|       } else {
00866|         await route.fulfill({

00868|           contentType: 'application/json',
00869|           body: JSON.stringify({ error: 'File not found' }),
00870|         });
00871|       }
00872|     } else if (method === 'PUT') {
00873|       // Mock file update
00874|       const body = route.request().postDataJSON();
00875|       const newSha = `sha-${Date.now()}`;
00876|

00879|         sha: newSha,

00882|

00885|         contentType: 'application/json',
00886|         body: JSON.stringify({
00887|           sha: newSha,
00888|           commit: `commit-${Date.now()}`,
00889|         }),
00890|       });
00891|     } else {

00893|     }

# Ralph Agent Instructions

You are an autonomous coding agent working on a software project.

## Your Task

1. Read the PRD at `prd.json` (in the same directory as this file)
2. Read the progress log at `progress.txt` (check Codebase Patterns section first)
3. Check you're on the correct branch from PRD `branchName`. If not, check it out or create from main.
4. Pick the **highest priority** user story where `passes: false`, and phase is `MVP`.
5. Implement that single user story **completely**
6. Run quality checks (e.g., typecheck, lint, test - use whatever your project requires)
7. **CRITICAL**: Verify ALL acceptance criteria are met using automated testing
8. Update AGENTS.md files if you discover reusable patterns (see below)
9. If **ALL** checks pass AND **ALL** acceptance criteria verified, commit with message: `feat: [Story ID] - [Story Title]`
10. **ONLY IF FULLY COMPLETE**: Update the PRD to set `passes: true` for the completed story
11. Append your progress to `progress.txt` with detailed notes


## IMPORTANT: Story Completion Rules

**A story is ONLY complete when:**
- ✅ All code is written
- ✅ All tests are written that assert the acceptance criteria (see Testing section)
- ✅ TypeScript type checking passes
- ✅ All tests pass
- ✅ Code is committed
- ✅ NO errors occurred during implementation

**If ANY acceptance criteria is NOT met:**
- ❌ Do NOT mark `passes: true` in the PRD
- ❌ Do NOT claim the story is complete
- ✅ Add detailed notes in the PRD explaining what's incomplete or what failed
- ✅ Document the issue in progress.txt

## Progress Report Format

APPEND to progress.txt (never replace, always append):
```
## [Date/Time] - [Story ID]
- What was implemented
- Files changed
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Patterns discovered (e.g., "this codebase uses X for Y")
  - Gotchas encountered (e.g., "don't forget to update Z when changing W")
  - Useful context (e.g., "the evaluation panel is in component X")
---
```

Include the thread URL so future iterations can use the `read_thread` tool to reference previous work if needed.

The learnings section is critical - it helps future iterations avoid repeating mistakes and understand the codebase better.

## Consolidate Patterns

If you discover a **reusable pattern** that future iterations should know, add it to the `## Codebase Patterns` section at the TOP of progress.txt (create it if it doesn't exist). This section should consolidate the most important learnings:

```
## Codebase Patterns
- Example: Use `sql<number>` template for aggregations
- Example: Always use `IF NOT EXISTS` for migrations
- Example: Export types from actions.ts for UI components
```

Only add patterns that are **general and reusable**, not story-specific details.

## Update AGENTS.md Files

Before committing, check if any edited files have learnings worth preserving in nearby AGENTS.md files:

1. **Identify directories with edited files** - Look at which directories you modified
2. **Check for existing AGENTS.md** - Look for AGENTS.md in those directories or parent directories
3. **Add valuable learnings** - If you discovered something future developers/agents should know:
   - API patterns or conventions specific to that module
   - Gotchas or non-obvious requirements
   - Dependencies between files
   - Testing approaches for that area
   - Configuration or environment requirements

**Examples of good AGENTS.md additions:**
- "When modifying X, also update Y to keep them in sync"
- "This module uses pattern Z for all API calls"
- "Tests require the dev server running on PORT 3000"
- "Field names must match the template exactly"

**Do NOT add:**
- Story-specific implementation details
- Temporary debugging notes
- Information already in progress.txt

Only update AGENTS.md if you have **genuinely reusable knowledge** that would help future work in that directory.

## Quality Requirements

- ALL commits must pass your project's quality checks (typecheck, lint, test)
- Do NOT commit broken code
- Keep changes focused and minimal
- Follow existing code patterns

## Testing

**1. Unit/Integration Tests** (Co-located with app: `apps/{app}/tests/`)
- **Framework**: Jest (backend), Vitest (frontend)
- **Purpose**: Fast, focused tests for business logic and components
- **Scope**: Single app, isolated units
- **Execution**: `npm test` from app directory

**2. App-Specific E2E Tests** (Co-located with app: `apps/{app}/tests/e2e/`)
- **Framework**: Playwright (browser), Supertest (API)
- **Purpose**: Complete user flows within single app
- **Scope**: Single app, full stack
- **Execution**: `npm run test:e2e` from app directory

**3. Cross-App Integration Tests** (Root level: `tests/`)
- **Framework**: Playwright
- **Purpose**: Multi-app workflows, authentication flows, end-to-end scenarios
- **Scope**: Multiple apps, complete system
- **Execution**: `npx playwright test` from repository root

### Testing Principles

**MUST follow these principles:**

1. **E2E First** - Start with broad end-to-end tests. Fewer tests, higher confidence.
2. **Align to Requirements** - Each test traces to a user story or requirement
3. **Mock Only Uncontrollable** - Use Docker for databases/storage. Mock only external APIs.
4. **Reset State** - Reset database/state before each test for isolation
5. **Unit Tests Later** - Add focused unit tests only after E2E coverage exists
6. **Minimise Duplication** - Share test utilities, avoid repeating test logic
7. **Descriptive Names** - ie: File: `user-authentication.e2e.test.ts`, Test: "should redirect to dashboard after successful login"

00001| import { Router, Request, Response } from 'express';
00002| import { authenticate } from '../middleware/authenticate.js';
00003| import { validateGitHubToken } from '../middleware/validateGitHubToken.js';
00004| import { GitHubService } from '../services/github.service.js';
00005| import { CommentFileService } from '../services/comment-file.service.js';
00006| import type { SessionUser } from '../config/passport.js';
00007| 
00008| const router = Router();
00009| const githubService = new GitHubService();
00010| const commentFileService = new CommentFileService();
00011| 
00012| /**
00013|  * POST /api/comments
00014|  * Create a new comment on a specific text range in a document
00015|  */
00016| router.post(
00017|   '/',
00018|   authenticate,
00019|   validateGitHubToken,
00020|   async (req: Request, res: Response) => {
00021|     try {
00022|       const { documentPath, repoOwner, repoName, charStart, charEnd, text } = req.body;
00023|       const user = req.user as SessionUser;
00024|       const userId = user?.id;
00025|       const githubToken = res.locals.githubToken;
00026| 
00027|       // Validation
00028|       if (!documentPath || !repoOwner || !repoName || charStart === undefined || charEnd === undefined || !text) {
00029|         return res.status(400).json({
00030|           error: 'Missing required fields: documentPath, repoOwner, repoName, charStart, charEnd, text'
00031|         });
00032|       }
00033| 
00034|       if (typeof charStart !== 'number' || typeof charEnd !== 'number') {
00035|         return res.status(400).json({
00036|           error: 'charStart and charEnd must be numbers'
00037|         });
00038|       }
00039| 
00040|       if (charStart < 0 || charEnd < charStart) {
00041|         return res.status(400).json({
00042|           error: 'Invalid character range: charStart must be >= 0 and charEnd must be >= charStart'
00043|         });
00044|       }
00045| 
00046|       if (!text.trim()) {
00047|         return res.status(400).json({
00048|           error: 'Comment text cannot be empty'
00049|         });
00050|       }
00051| 
00052|       // Fetch or create comment file
00053|       const existingFile = await githubService.getCommentFile(
00054|         repoOwner,
00055|         repoName,
00056|         documentPath,
00057|         githubToken,
00058|         req.logger
00059|       );
00060| 
00061|       let commentData = existingFile
00062|         ? commentFileService.parseCommentFile(existingFile.content, req.logger)
00063|         : commentFileService.createEmptyCommentFile(documentPath);
00064| 
00065|       // Add comment
00066|       const { data: updatedData, commentId } = commentFileService.addComment(commentData, {
00067|         charStart,
00068|         charEnd,
00069|         author: {
00070|           username: user.username,
00071|           avatarUrl: user.avatarUrl,
00072|         },
00073|         text: text.trim(),
00074|         resolved: false,
00075|       });
00076| 
00077|       // Serialize and save
00078|       const fileContent = commentFileService.serializeCommentFile(updatedData);
00079|       await githubService.saveCommentFile(
00080|         repoOwner,
00081|         repoName,
00082|         documentPath,
00083|         fileContent,
00084|         existingFile?.sha || null,
00085|         `Add comment on ${documentPath}`,
00086|         githubToken,
00087|         req.logger
00088|       );
00089| 
00090|       const newComment = commentFileService.getComment(updatedData, commentId);
00091| 
00092|       req.logger?.info('Comment created successfully', {
00093|         userId,
00094|         commentId,
00095|         repoOwner,
00096|         repoName,
00097|         documentPath,
00098|         operation: 'create_comment'
00099|       });
00100| 
00101|       // Return in API format for backward compatibility
00102|       const apiComment = commentFileService.convertToApiFormat(newComment!, userId);
00103|       apiComment.documentPath = documentPath;
00104|       apiComment.repoOwner = repoOwner;
00105|       apiComment.repoName = repoName;
00106| 
00107|       res.status(201).json(apiComment);
00108|     } catch (error) {
00109|       req.logger?.error('Failed to create comment', error as Error, {
00110|         userId: (req.user as SessionUser)?.id,
00111|         operation: 'create_comment'
00112|       });
00113|       res.status(500).json({ error: 'Failed to create comment' });
00114|     }
00115|   }
00116| );
00117| 
00118| /**
00119|  * POST /api/comments/:commentId/replies
00120|  * Create a reply to a comment
00121|  */
00122| router.post(

import { describe, it, expect } from '@jest/globals';

describe('Comment Feature', () => {
  describe('Comment validation logic', () => {
    it('should validate character range correctly', () => {
      const charStart = 0;
      const charEnd = 10;

      expect(charStart >= 0).toBe(true);
      expect(charEnd >= charStart).toBe(true);
    });

    it('should reject negative character start', () => {
      const invalidStart = -1;
      expect(invalidStart < 0).toBe(true);
    });

    it('should reject invalid range where end < start', () => {
      const validStart = 10;
      const invalidEnd = 5;
      expect(invalidEnd < validStart).toBe(true);
    });

    it('should validate that text is not empty', () => {
      const text = 'This is a comment';
      expect(text.trim()).not.toBe('');
    });

    it('should reject empty or whitespace-only text', () => {
      const emptyText = '   ';
      expect(emptyText.trim()).toBe('');
    });
  });

  describe('Comment data transformation', () => {
    it('should map database rows to comment objects correctly', () => {
      const row = {
        id: 1,
        user_id: 1,
        document_path: 'docs/README.md',
        repo_owner: 'testowner',
        repo_name: 'testrepo',
        char_start: 0,
        char_end: 10,
        text: 'Test comment',
        resolved: false,
        created_at: new Date(),
        updated_at: new Date(),
        username: 'testuser',
        avatar_url: 'https://github.com/testuser.png',
      };

      const comment = {
        id: row.id,
        userId: row.user_id,
        documentPath: row.document_path,
        repoOwner: row.repo_owner,
        repoName: row.repo_name,
        charStart: row.char_start,
        charEnd: row.char_end,
        text: row.text,
        resolved: row.resolved,
        createdAt: row.created_at,
        updatedAt: row.updated_at,
        user: {
          id: row.user_id,
          username: row.username,
          avatarUrl: row.avatar_url,
        },
      };

      expect(comment.id).toBe(row.id);
      expect(comment.charStart).toBe(row.char_start);
      expect(comment.charEnd).toBe(row.char_end);
      expect(comment.user.username).toBe(row.username);
      expect(comment.user.avatarUrl).toBe(row.avatar_url);
    });

        charStart: mockRow.char_start,
        charEnd: mockRow.char_end,
        text: mockRow.text,
        resolved: mockRow.resolved,
        createdAt: mockRow.created_at,
        updatedAt: mockRow.updated_at,
        user: {
          id: mockRow.user_id,
          username: mockRow.username,
          avatarUrl: mockRow.avatar_url,
        },
      };

      expect(transformed).toHaveProperty('charEnd', 15);
      expect(transformed.user).toHaveProperty('username', 'john');
    });
  });

      ];

      const sorted = [...comments].sort((a, b) => {
        if (a.char_start !== b.char_start) {
          return a.char_start - b.char_start;
        }
        return a.created_at.getTime() - b.created_at.getTime();
      });

      expect(sorted[0].id).toBe(1);

      expect(sorted[2].id).toBe(3);
    });
